description: Trigger discrimination for agent-instruction-consolidator against the nearest shipped owners.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. Our root CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md disagree about the test command; consolidate them to one canonical source.
cases.reason: Both files are agent-instruction files, which is this skill's scope; source-of-truth-reconciler reconciles documents against code, which this skill's Do NOT use when excludes.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. We just adopted Cursor; inventory every instruction file and propose one canonical source.
cases.reason: Adopting a new AI tool is a named trigger in Use When; docs-as-code-architect builds the documentation pipeline, not the per-tool instruction map.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. Our Cursor rules and AGENTS.md carry duplicated content that has drifted apart.
cases.reason: The duplication is between instruction files; agent-memory-governance governs what an agent retains, not what it is told before it starts.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. Audit our agent instruction files for drift and duplication before we add another tool.
cases.reason: The deliverable is the inventory, conflict matrix and consolidation proposal; the startup gate decides what is loaded, not whether the files agree.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. We have root and nested CLAUDE.md overrides plus Copilot instructions; consolidate to one canonical file with thin pointers.
cases.reason: Nested overrides are instruction-file precedence, which this skill's Gotchas own; context-window packing is a different design task.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. Build the rule-by-file conflict matrix across AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, the Cursor rules and the Copilot instructions.
cases.reason: The conflict matrix is this skill's own artifact; agent-harness-architect designs the tool surface, permissions and loop instead.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. Two instruction files now contradict each other on style rules after a merge.
cases.reason: The merge left no damaged tree, only disagreeing instruction files; code-reviewer assesses a diff and cannot choose a canonical instruction source.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-instruction-consolidator. Show me the rule-preservation diff for every rule before you edit any instruction file.
cases.reason: The rule-preservation diff is this skill's proposal artifact; reviewable-diff-discipline shapes commits for review, not a rule inventory.

cases.prompt: The documentation claims the API retries three times and the code retries five; reconcile the documentation to the code.
cases.reason: Docs-versus-code reconciliation is the boundary named in this skill's Do NOT use when, which routes it to source-of-truth-reconciler.

cases.prompt: Set up our docs-as-code pipeline: linting, review gates and generated reference pages.
cases.reason: This builds documentation tooling; it does not touch agent instruction files.

cases.prompt: Rewrite the repository README front page so a newcomer can start in five minutes.
cases.reason: A README for humans is not an agent instruction file and has no cross-tool consolidation surface.

cases.prompt: Decide what context an agent should load at session start, and in what order.
cases.reason: The question is what is loaded and when, not whether several instruction files agree with each other.

cases.prompt: Design the agent harness: tool surface, permission model and loop termination.
cases.reason: Harness design is runtime capability, not instruction text.

cases.prompt: Design the context-window budget and packing strategy for long sessions.
cases.reason: Context budgeting is a separate design task; no instruction file is inventoried or merged.

cases.prompt: Audit our agent memory store for poisoning and stale entries.
cases.reason: Memory content is runtime state, not the instruction files this skill consolidates.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke prompt-injection-defender. Our AGENTS.md contains a suspicious instruction payload; assess whether it is an injection attempt.
cases.reason: The nearest boundary here: the file is an instruction file, but the finding is hostile content, and consolidation would carry the payload into the canonical copy. Security assessment comes first.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-goal-hijack-defender. The agent's goal drifted away from the assigned task during a long run.
cases.reason: Drift inside a run is a runtime goal-integrity problem; the instruction files may be perfectly consistent.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-memory-governance. Define what an agent may store, for how long, and who may change it.
cases.reason: Retention and change authority over memory is a governance ruleset, not a consolidation of instruction files.

cases.prompt: Write the CONTRIBUTING guide for outside contributors.
cases.reason: A contributor guide is human-facing process documentation, not tool instruction files.

cases.prompt: Restructure the documentation into tutorials, how-to guides, reference and explanation.
cases.reason: Documentation taxonomy is not agent-instruction consolidation, even though both act on prose files.

cases.prompt: Review this pull request diff for correctness and missing tests.
cases.reason: A code review is not an instruction-file audit, and consolidation is additionally manual-only.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke agent-authorization-matrix. Define what each agent role is allowed to do.
cases.reason: Permissions per role are an authorization matrix; instruction files may describe them but this skill does not define authority.

cases.prompt: Explicitly invoke aegis-setup. Install the Aegis skills and instruction files into this consumer repository for the first time.
cases.reason: Found by the topic sweep of all 255 shipped descriptions rather than by picking a convenient strawman: it also writes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. A first install CREATES one truth; consolidation reconciles several already-present ones, which is why the skill's Do NOT use when excludes a repo with no instruction file.

seam_note: agent-instruction-consolidator <-> agent-failure-recovery: the two manual-only skills shipped together in this batch. A bad merge whose only residue is DISAGREEING INSTRUCTION FILES is consolidation (this file's positive-1 and positive-7); a bad merge that left a DAMAGED TREE is recovery. Both directions are pinned: agent-failure-recovery-negative-14 pins the reciprocal boundary. Manual-only, so every case expecting either skill uses the strict prefix 'Explicitly invoke <skill>. '.
